reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator 'weather_scenario_modulation' defines a stochastic process where activity schedules A(t) evolve according to probabilistic weather events w(t). This is modeled as a conditional expectation E[U(A(t), w(t)) | w(t)] which induces a Bayesian update mechanism. The 'bayesian_climate_inference' primitive formalizes how prior beliefs about weather P(H) are updated to posterior beliefs P(H|E) using likelihood P(E|H). The 'utility_conditional_planning' primitive then evaluates expected utility over these conditioned scenarios. Dualities emerge in that weather forecasting and activity planning form a feedback loop: better forecasts improve utility estimates, while utility-driven decisions inform future weather modeling. Failure modes include overfitting to historical weather patterns, leading to brittle activity plans when novel weather occurs. The system's robustness depends on the richness of the weather ensemble and the expressiveness of the utility function.
